draft.title: Using your voice in a presentation
card: Volume
how loud or soft you speak. Speak loudly enough for the back of the room to hear.
Tone
the feeling in your voice, such as excited, serious or friendly. It should suit your message.
Pitch
how high or low your voice sounds. Changing pitch stops your voice sounding flat.
Pace
how fast you speak. Slow down for important points and pause so listeners can take them in.
draft.remember: Changing your voice holds attention and makes your meaning clear.

a.q: Zoe is giving a talk and speaks slowly and pauses before her main point so listeners can take it in. Which part of her voice is she changing?
opts: Pace
Volume
Pitch
Tone
a.why: Pace is how fast a speaker talks, and Zoe slows down and pauses. Volume is about loudness, which she did not change.

b.q: Noah gives a talk about a sad story of a lost dog. He speaks in a bright, cheerful voice the whole time. What is the main problem?
opts: His tone does not suit the message
His pace is too slow for the audience
His volume is too soft to be heard
His pitch is too low for the room
b.why: Tone is the feeling in the voice, and a cheerful tone does not match a sad story. The problem is not stated as speed, loudness or pitch.
b.clue: Match the feeling of the voice to the story.

b.best: His tone does not suit the message

Pace
how fast you speak. Slow down for important points and pause so listeners can take them in.
proposal.remember: Changing your voice holds attention and makes your meaning clear.

a.q: Zoe rushes through her opening, then takes her time over her last sentence and stops briefly before her main point. Which part of her voice is she changing?
opts: Pace
Volume
Pitch
Tone
a.why: Pace is how fast a speaker talks. Zoe goes from rushing to taking her time, and she pauses, so she changes her pace. Volume is about loudness, and nothing suggests she spoke louder or softer.
a.clue: Compare her opening with her last sentence. What is different?

b.why: Tone is the feeling in the voice, and a cheerful tone does not match a sad story. Nothing in the scenario says he spoke too slowly, too softly or too low.
b.clue: Match the feeling of the voice to the story.
